title: Conduct Adjustment to the Young-Driver Surcharge Rate: Miles Driven Against the Allowance Granted
content:
Percentage points go onto the young-driver surcharge rate on a Keyturn Trip Booking where the reservation's odometer readings show the included-mile allowance being used up heavily, and only once the trip has been running for at least 7 days.

**Where the reservation's odometer readings have booked more miles than the included miles granted to it, whatever those miles were granted for, and the trip has run for at least 7 days**, the conduct adjustment is 3 percentage points on.

**Where those readings have booked more than three quarters of the included miles granted to the reservation — more than 0.75 of that allowance — but not more than that allowance, and the trip has run for at least 7 days**, the conduct adjustment is 1 percentage point on.

**In every other case** no conduct adjustment is made, which is to say the adjustment is 0.

### What is counted, and how the days are counted

The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

The included miles granted to the reservation are every grant of included miles standing on its mileage record, whatever those miles were granted for.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The bands, on both of their sides

| Miles the readings have booked, against the included miles granted | Days the trip has run | Conduct adjustment (percentage points) |
|---|---|---|
| More than the allowance granted | 7 or more | 3 |
| More than three quarters of it but not more than it | 7 or more | 1 |
| Three quarters of it or less | 7 or more | 0 |
| Any | Fewer than 7 | 0 |

Both boundaries are passed rather than reached. Readings booking exactly the allowance granted are not more than it, so they fall in the middle band and give 1 percentage point. Readings booking exactly three quarters of the allowance are not more than three quarters of it, so they fall outside both bands and give 0. Seven days is reached rather than passed.

*Hypothetical.* A reservation granted 2000 included miles whose readings have booked 2300 miles, on a trip that has been running 15 days: the readings exceed the allowance and the first band gives 3 percentage points. The same reservation with 1700 miles booked — more than 1500 miles, which is three quarters of the allowance, and not more than 2000 — gives 1 percentage point. The same reservation with 1400 miles booked gives 0. A trip running only 4 days gives 0 whatever its readings show.
